name: ECOS (India) Mobility & Hospitality Ltd
title: ECOS (India) Mobility & Hospitality Ltd - 544239 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Asset-light corporate mobility grew trips 29% to 5.23m, but EBITDA margin fell to about 11.6% on ETS price competition and cost build; management guides 11-13% margin and 18-20% growth.

summary.headline: ECOS Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.65% to INR2,067.6 million, EBITDA down to INR241.5 million; FY27 guided to 18-20% growth at 11-13% margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 16.65% YoY to INR2,067.60 million, while EBITDA declined to INR241.53 million from INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25, reflecting continued investment in people, technology and leadership. For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Management said the Middle East crisis dented CCR growth in March, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and EBITDA margin of 11-13%, with cost growth expected to be lower than revenue growth. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR264.67 million in Q4 FY25 (decline)
vs 4.04 million in FY25, approx. +29% YoY

segments.name: ETS (employee transportation services)
segments.commentary: 58% of FY26 revenue and 57% in Q4 FY26. Stable demand from IT/ITES and a strong surge from GCC clients, but competitive pricing pressure was most visible here.

segments.name: CCR (chauffeur-driven car rental)
segments.commentary: 42% of FY26 revenue and 43% in Q4 FY26. Growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, though management says it bounced back; management described CCR as a brand-led business with a premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth aspiration of 18% to 20%; management expects about 60-65% of growth from new client acquisition and the rest from existing clients.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 11% to 13%, with management saying this holds for the next couple of years too.
Employee cost growth budgeted at about 13% to 16% in the latest AOP; other expenses to rise about 8% to 9%.
Fuel price increases above roughly 5% are generally passed through to clients, with lags of a few days to a few weeks.
No dividend declared; the board will hold a separate meeting to consider dividend or other ways to enhance shareholder value.
capex_capacity: FY26 vendor partner network of about 20,000 vehicles, versus about 14,000 in FY25; the model remains asset-light.
Over 14% of CCR corporate bookings came through CabDrive Pro, API or the customer app in Q4 FY26.
Direct web booking portal launched in Q4 FY26 for pre-scheduled rides, aimed at premium individuals and SMEs rather than mass B2C.
New core backend platform launched to improve process efficiency.

EV investment remains cautious; capex would rise materially only if EVs become financially sustainable and charging infrastructure and residual values support them. Analyst noted about INR120 million capex over four years (about INR30 million a year).
demand_pricing: Active client base above 1,750; 223 new clients added in FY26 (64 in Q4) versus 188 in FY25.
55% of FY26 revenue from clients associated with ECOS for more than five years. Churn among top 200 clients is about 2-3%, per management.
Demand from GCCs and manufacturing facilities is a notable driver of ETS enterprise wins; CCR growth is diversified across sectors.
Competitive price pressure is mainly in ETS, led by new entrants; management says prices should rise once operations prove unsustainable.

Average revenue per trip fell from about INR1,600 in FY25 to about INR1,550 in FY26, versus about INR1,750-1,780 in FY24. Management cited pricing pressure plus shorter ETS trips and more CCR airport transfers.
No demand impact seen yet from the government's work-from-home appeal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the West Asia crisis affecting demand, and what is FY27 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CCR growth slowed in March after the Middle East crisis, with a bounce back expected if the disruption is short. Management aspires to 18-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can fuel price hikes be passed on, and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Most contracts have pass-through clauses triggered above roughly 5%, with lags of days to weeks. Management says the 6-7% increase has been fully passed on.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the INR8 crore receivable provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal proceedings for recovery are ongoing and management is hopeful. Recovery may come in FY27 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected growth rates for employee and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is budgeted to grow about 13-16% and other expenses about 8-9%, both below the revenue growth target. Management expects operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue per trip declining, and is pricing pressure easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ETS pricing pressure and shorter trips plus airport transfers. Pressure appears to have stabilised in the last quarter, while the company is also winning larger enterprise contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to the earlier 14-16% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 11-13% for FY27 and the next couple of years. It expects CCR brand premium to offset ETS price competition over time.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin in FY26 was about 11.6%, down from roughly 15% at IPO, and Q4 EBITDA fell YoY despite 16.65% revenue growth.
Falling revenue per trip (about INR1,550 in FY26) indicates pricing pressure in ETS from new entrants.
Pending legal recovery of the roughly INR80 million doubtful debt; timing is uncertain.
Middle East and fuel-price volatility affecting CCR demand and the lag in fuel pass-through.
Cost growth versus revenue growth in FY27: the company needs to deliver operating leverage against its 13-16% employee cost budget.
Dividend decision pending a separate board meeting.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and client wins, but cautious on near-term margins and EV capex. Management was candid that pricing pressure in ETS and the March CCR slowdown weighed on the quarter, and it avoided quantifying the timing of margin recovery beyond guidance.
key_quotes: So, we have to focus on both and we have to see how we are able to draw a balance between the growing the revenue and also expanding the margins.
So, that was a one-time and we have already that is under legal proceedings for recovery of that money and we are very hopeful of the recovery.
I cannot sacrifice revenue growth for expanding the margin in any one year because then I'm compromising my business for the future.

growth.why: Management "aspires" to 18-20% FY27 revenue growth with 11-13% EBITDA margin, backed by new-client acquisition (60-65% of growth) and a 20,000-vehicle asset-light partner network, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts with numbers or timing were given.
